description: Team VEGA is competing in NASA Space Apps 2026 (Giza) for "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts". We're building an IoT & AI health pod merging wearable biosensors with an analytical dashboard to track astronaut vitals autonomously.
summary:
ASTRO-GUARD (VEGA): Astronaut Health Monitor

NASA Space Apps 2026 prototype (not a medical device).

Idea

A wearable system that monitors an astronaut’s vitals, surroundings, and motion, and streams the data to a computer dashboard and a phone.

Device (ESP32)

Sensors: MAX30102 (heart rate, SpO2), DS18B20 (temperature), MQ-2 (gas), flame sensor, MPU-6050 (motion).
Outputs: OLED, LCD, buzzer, 3 buttons, HC-05 Bluetooth.

Features:

Health score out of 100 with three alert levels (normal, warning, danger)
Gas leak and fire detection
Fall detection (free-fall, impact, then lying still); the alert stays on until “I’m OK” is pressed
Stress alert when mood is “stressed” and heart rate is above 100
Blood sugar and mood received from the dashboard or phone
XP and activity tracking, plus a 15-minute routine reminder
7 display pages: Home, Vitals, Environment, Motion, Trend, Check-in, Crew
Sends JSON data over USB serial and Bluetooth
Dashboard (VEGA web page)
Connects to the device by serial, or runs in simulation mode
Live cards, charts, and progress rings for all sensors
Motion and fall card with an “I’m OK” button
Event log, data table, and audio alarms
Manual daily check-in (blood sugar, mood) sent back to the device
Health guidance based on the readings
Result

The device measures and alerts, the dashboard displays and logs, and both use the same alert thresholds.
details:
What it does: ASTRO-GUARD is a wearable health and safety monitor for astronauts. An ESP32 reads pulse and SpO2 (MAX30102), temperature (DS18B20), gas (MQ-2), flame, and motion (MPU-6050). It calculates a health score, detects falls, and raises alerts on the suit's OLED, LCD, and buzzer. Data streams over USB and Bluetooth to VEGA, a web dashboard with live charts, an event log, and health guidance. Astronauts log blood sugar and mood there, and the values return to the device.

Benefits and impact: Early warning of health problems, gas leaks, fire, and falls, even when the crew cannot look at a screen. It supports autonomy on long missions where contact with Earth is delayed. It could also help firefighters, hazardous-site workers, and the elderly on Earth.

Tools: Arduino C++ (Adafruit, OneWire, SparkFun libraries), HTML/CSS/JavaScript with the Web Serial API, and HC-05 Bluetooth.

Creativity: Sensor fusion (a stressed mood plus high heart rate triggers an alert), two-way device-dashboard communication, a three-stage fall detector (free-fall, impact, lying still), XP gamification to encourage healthy habits, and a simulation mode that works without hardware.

Factors considered: Low cost, non-blocking code so alerts never stall, identical thresholds on device and dashboard, sensor calibration, and honest limits: it is a prototype, not a medical device.
